reviews.title: Industrialized Progression Is Hurting the Game
reviews.text:
The game has some genuinely interesting mechanics, but the economy and progression systems feel increasingly distorted because multi-accounting is effectively normalized.

There are rules meant to limit direct interaction between alts, yet players can still indirectly funnel resources and gold through market systems and coordinated production chains. The end result is that some individuals or groups scale XP, crafting, and wealth at levels that normal players realistically cannot compete with.

At some point it stops feeling like an MMO economy and starts feeling like competing against private industrial networks.

The issue is less about any single player and more about a system that unintentionally rewards account scaling far more than actual gameplay balance.

reviews.text: I’ve been a dedicated player of War Shovel for a long time, but I can no longer support it. Over the past two years, the game has become increasingly exploitative, with every essential feature locked behind massive paywalls. The developer has also completely turned a blind eye to player concerns—no bug fixes, no balance changes, and just complete silence on in-game issues. reviews.title: Fun game with lots of options
reviews.text: It is easy to get started with Warshovel. The tutorial is also useful in the beginning. You set up all of your processes in the Game handles them for you overtime. For example, exploring and crafting all happen in the background. It is really fun to log back onto the game and see your AFK rewards of experience and items you collect. You can specialize in different areas of crafting such as Alchemy, cooking, blacksmithing, tailoring, and so forth. I am very excited to see what I can achieve at higher levels. This is a fun game that you can check in on as often or as little as you want. However, the free version only lets you be off-line for eight hours. I haven’t figured out what happens if you were away from the game more than that. It does offer a monthly subscription service so you can invest in the game if you want or just enjoy playing the free version. Overall, a nice game.
